full_judgment:
Mr. Mir Hashmat Ali, J.:- The petitioner Hajee Md. Khorshed Ali Mutawalli of Khan Shaheb Hajee Emdad Ali Waqf Estate challenged the judgment and order No.71 dated 03.07.2008 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Appeal No.10 of 1993 passed under Section 36 of the Waqf's Ordinance. 

 2. The Opposite party Nos.1-9 preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.10 of 1993 on 14.01.1993 before the Court of District Judge, Dhaka against the order dated 21.09.1992 passed by Administrator of Waqf of Bangladesh alleging and claiming that they have approximately 4 annas secular and undivided share used to manage together with the properties belonging to Waqf Estate under E.C. No.1400. But since after the appointment of Mutawalli of the present petitioner, the secular undivided 4 annas share including the share of Waqf Property has not been running properly for mal-administration of respondent No.2 petitioner. The said opposite parties also filed an application to the Administrator of Waqf to distribute their undivided share by determining the waqf property. Thereafter the said Miscellaneous Appeal No.10 of 1993 was allowed vide order dated 21.09.1992 and the order of Administrator of Waqf of Bangladesh has been vacated vide judgment and order dated 29.11.1993 by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka. Thereafter on receipt of the aforesaid order, the respondent-opposite party No.10 issued letter under Memo No. ওঃপঃ/ঢাঃদঃ/৭৯ তারিখঃ ১২/০৮/২০০৩ and ওঃপ্রঃ/ঢাঃদঃ/৩৫০ তারিখঃ ১৮/০৩/২০০৪ upon the present petitioner. 

 10. Mr. Md. Rezaul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioner submitted that the opposite parties have filed an Execution Case No.1 of 2006 before the Court of Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, which was rejected on 29.11.1993 and said order is not executable order. He further submits that after 15 years the opposite parties filed an application for precept under Section 46 of the Code of Civil Procedure, which was subsequently transferred to the Court of Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka and marked and numbered as Miscellaneous Appeal No.10 of 1993. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that there is an order of ad-interim injunction granted on 06.08.2006 in Civil Revision No.2743 of 2006, which is still pending before the Court for violation of the order. The contempt Rule has been issued in Civil Rule No.612(R)/2007 (Contempt) and during the pendency of the contempt rule the opposite parties filed an application for precept by violating the order of injunction dated 06.08.2006 for which another Contempt Rule being Civil Rule No.390(R) of 2008 (Contempt) Rule has been issued. But the Court below passed the impugned order by violating the order of this Court and thereby committed an offence of Contempt of Court resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that the opposite parties filed an application for perception under Section 46 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the said Miscellaneous Appeal No.10 of 1993 for execution of the judgment and order dated 29.11.1993, which has been subsequently modified on 26.10.2004. But the learned Additional District Judge while disposing the said Miscellaneous Appeal No.10 of 1993, the learned District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka issued precept upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka. 

 11. Mr. Abdus Salam appearing with Mrs. Ambia Bulbul Rezia and Mr. Humayon Kabir Sikder, the learned Advocates for the opposite parties by filing counter affidavit submits that the petitioner incorporated several facts, which are not at all necessary for proper adjudication of the impugned order dated 03.07.2008 and Civil Revision No.2743 of 2006 filed by the petitioner was heard and disposed of by this Court on 09.01.2011 by holding that the petitioner filed the suit in a wrong forum. Further stating that the Court below after considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record rightly passed the impugned order. In support of his contention, he has produced Photostat of two certified copies of the judgment passed in Title Suit No.34 of 1964 arises out of Title Suit No.9 of 1963 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka. 

 12. Mr. Md. Rezaul Islam, the learned Advocate on reply submits that the petitioner are not oppose to demarcate the waqf property with the property of private individual which are kept outside of the waqf estate. But some of the co-sharer has already compromised with them and as such their interest is also to be considered. He further submits that since Miscellaneous Appeal No.10 of 1993 is not a case to be executed and as such the order passed under Section 46 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not applicable. 

 14. It appears that Syeda Fatema Faizun Nessa filed an application before the Waqf Administrator in E.C. No.1400 claiming 4 annas share of the rent and also prayed for demarcation of the property as the entire property was not the Waqf Property and that the petitioners obtained some share from their predecessor and that they are entitled to get the share of 3 anna 18 ganda 2 kara 2 kranti. But after the appointment of Mr. Abdul Quader as Mutawalli no share of payment of rent was paid to the heirs of the Waqif. The Administrator of Waqf issued notice upon the Mutawalli. The Mutawalli filed written objection stating that since their share has not been determined by demarcation of the property. They have to file a suit for partition and they can obtain their property by determining the area of the land. The Waqf Administrator made an enquiry and Assistant Waqf Administrator filed a report on 16.12.1991 and on 06.09.1992 an application was filed before the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to demarcate the share. Subsequently Mutawalli filed an application to the High Court Division that a proceeding is pending before the High Court Division and High Court Division stayed all further proceeding vide order dated 28.09.1992. Waqf's Administrator stayed the matter. Against which the said Syeda Fatima Faizun Nessa filed Miscellaneous Appeal No.10 of 1993 before the District Judge, Dhaka, which was eventually transferred to the Court of Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka. 

 17. It appears that there is no conflict between waqf property and personal property and no suit or case is pending regarding the same. The learned Advocate for the Mutawalli admitted that the opposite parties are entitled to get 3 annas 18 ganda 2 kara 2 kranti share and that no demarcation has yet been made. Since no execution case is maintainable in that case the order of precept to the Deputy Commissioner is a proper forum to demarcate the property of the Waqf property from the personal property and as such I find that the judgment and order dated 03.07.2008 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Appeal No.10 of 1993 is a proper order and in accordance with law and such order does not calls for any interference by this Revisional Court.
